description: The statement by which an operator key declares an HTTPS origin's host name, and the checks a third party performs on it. The operator key signs the statement; the origin publishes it; anyone holding the operator identifier checks that both declare each other. Not part of an independence proof and no input to its verification.

rules.signed_payload: JCS (RFC 8785) of the statement without signature_alg and signature_b64.
rules.signed_message: The ASCII prefix `certcrypt:operator-domain-binding:1|` followed by the signed payload (operator.recognition/1 §10).
rules.statement_digest: SHA3-256 of the signed payload. With (operator_id, sequence) it is the statement's identity; signature_alg and signature_b64 are outside it.
rules.signature: ML-DSA-65 (FIPS 204), empty context, by the operator key over the signed message, standard base64. The signatures here use the deterministic variant so the files reproduce; a conforming signer may hedge, so an implementation verifies signatures and compares bytes only for what is deterministic.
rules.rule_ids: Each refusal names the clause that decides it: 4-members (member set, duplicate names, types), 4-values (fixed values and formats), 5-* (host name; 5-public-suffix is the ICANN Public Suffix List rule), 6-operator-id, 6-signature, 7.1-order, 7.1-bind-max-validity, 7.1-future, 7.1-expired, 7.2-sequence.

construction.what_it_checks: From fixed inputs, the exact bytes a producer signs and a consumer recomputes. The key is the FIPS 204 key generated from seed_hex (the seed is the 32-byte xi).

cases.label: bind
cases.what_it_shows: A bind valid for exactly 90 days. The typed host name is upper case with a trailing dot; the statement carries its canonical form.

tampered.what_it_shows: Bit 0 of byte 100 of the signature flipped; nothing else changed. It must not verify.

cases.label: bind-same-sequence-other-content
cases.what_it_shows: Same operator and sequence as `bind`, one day shorter: a different statement_digest under the same identity pair, which is what §7.2 calls a conflict.

cases.label: unbind
cases.what_it_shows: The withdrawal of `bind`, one sequence higher.

cases.label: first-bind
cases.what_it_shows: The first statement of a key: sequence 1, issued at the instant it is signed, valid for the 90-day maximum. A node that signs its first bind for this host at T0 produces exactly this signed payload.

cases.label: bind-idn
cases.what_it_shows: An internationalized host name, carried as its A-label after UTS #46 processing (mapping folds the case).

cases.label: bind-other-operator
cases.what_it_shows: Another operator key declaring the same host, as during a change of operator key (§8.1).

cases.label: bind-other-host
cases.what_it_shows: The same operator key declaring another host name.

cases.label: bind-earlier
cases.what_it_shows: A bind of the same host below `bind`, never accepted: what a replay of an older statement looks like.

statement_validity.what_it_checks: Every check of §4 to §7.1 a consumer makes on one statement at instant `now`, with no state: the member set parsed from the exact JSON text, the values, the host name, operator_id against the carried key, the signature under that key, and the validity window. Each refused case breaks one rule and keeps the others; where a case changes a signed member it is signed again, so the signature does not decide it.

cases.label: valid-bind
cases.what_it_shows: The `bind` construction case, checked inside its window.

cases.label: bind-90-days-plus-one-second
cases.what_it_shows: valid_until one second beyond 90 days after issued_at.

cases.label: unbind-91-days
cases.what_it_shows: The 90-day limit applies to a bind only.

cases.label: issued-at-equals-valid-until
cases.what_it_shows: issued_at must be strictly earlier than valid_until.

cases.label: unbind-valid-until-before-issued-at
cases.what_it_shows: The order rule applies to an unbind too.

cases.label: issued-at-five-minutes-ahead
cases.what_it_shows: issued_at exactly five minutes after now is within the tolerance.

cases.label: issued-at-beyond-tolerance
cases.what_it_shows: issued_at five minutes and one second after now.

cases.label: last-second-of-window
cases.what_it_shows: now one second before valid_until.

cases.label: expired-at-valid-until
cases.what_it_shows: now equal to valid_until: the window is half-open (§10.1 intervals end at valid_until, §10.2).

cases.label: unbind-expired
cases.what_it_shows: An unbind whose valid_until has passed can no longer be accepted for the first time (§7.3).

cases.label: sequence-leading-zero
cases.what_it_shows: A decimal string without leading zeros.

cases.label: sequence-zero
cases.what_it_shows: The lowest sequence is 1.

cases.label: sequence-above-maximum
cases.what_it_shows: One above 2^53 - 1.

cases.label: sequence-at-maximum
cases.what_it_shows: Exactly 2^53 - 1.

cases.label: sequence-as-json-number
cases.what_it_shows: A member of the wrong type. The signature is the original one: the statement is refused before it is checked.

cases.label: issued-at-fractional-seconds
cases.what_it_shows: Instants carry whole seconds and no fraction.

cases.label: issued-at-with-offset
cases.what_it_shows: The same instant written with an offset: instants are UTC with `Z`.

cases.label: missing-member
cases.what_it_shows: domain_binding_method absent. The original signature is kept; the member set is checked first.

cases.label: additional-member
cases.what_it_shows: A member outside the closed set of §4.

cases.label: duplicate-member-same-value
cases.what_it_shows: `intent` twice with the same value. A duplicate member name is refused whatever the values.

cases.label: duplicate-member-other-value
cases.what_it_shows: `domain_ascii` twice with different values: a parser that keeps the last one would see the signed host.

cases.label: intent-outside-set
cases.what_it_shows: intent is `bind` or `unbind`.

cases.label: method-outside-set
cases.what_it_shows: `https-well-known` is the only method of /1, and it is under the signature.

cases.label: artifact-type-other-version
cases.what_it_shows: Another artifact type.

cases.label: signature-alg-other
cases.what_it_shows: signature_alg is outside the signed payload, so the signature still verifies; the value is refused on its own.

cases.label: signature-not-base64
cases.what_it_shows: signature_b64 is standard base64.

cases.label: operator-id-not-derived
cases.what_it_shows: operator_id of another key, signed correctly by the carried key.

cases.label: public-key-of-another-operator
cases.what_it_shows: The key and signature of operator-b under operator-a's identifier: the signature verifies, the identifier does not derive from the key.

cases.label: host-name-not-canonical
cases.what_it_shows: A carried host name with an upper-case letter, correctly signed.

cases.label: host-name-is-icann-public-suffix
cases.what_it_shows: A carried host name that is itself a public suffix of the ICANN section, correctly signed.

cases.label: signature-bit-flipped
cases.what_it_shows: The tampered copy of the construction case.

cases.label: payload-changed-after-signing
cases.what_it_shows: domain_ascii changed after signing, signature kept.

cases.label: signed-without-prefix
cases.what_it_shows: A valid signature over signed_payload_jcs alone, without the domain-separation prefix. It verifies over those bytes and not over the signed message.

cases.label: signed-under-another-prefix
cases.what_it_shows: A valid signature under a prefix of another version.

cases.label: signed-by-another-key
cases.what_it_shows: Signed by operator-b, carrying operator-a's key and identifier.

non_public_top_level_names.what_it_shows: Every top-level name §5 lists as never resolving in the public DNS. Build `node.<name>` for each: a producer refuses it as input and a consumer refuses it as a carried domain_ascii. The names are listed rather than spelled out as host names.

public_suffix_list_excerpt.what_it_shows: The Public Suffix List rules the carried cases depend on, by section. A consumer uses the full list; these rules have been stable in it for years and are enough to recompute every `5-public-suffix` case with the standard algorithm (longest matching rule, exceptions win, default rule `*`).

input_cases.label: trailing-dot
input_cases.what_it_shows: The carried form has no trailing dot.

input_cases.label: idn-upper-case
input_cases.what_it_shows: Case folding happens before the conversion.

input_cases.label: idn-non-transitional
input_cases.what_it_shows: Non-transitional processing keeps U+00DF; transitional processing would have produced `fass`.

input_cases.label: a-label-input
input_cases.what_it_shows: An A-label typed as such is kept.

input_cases.label: check-hyphens-third-fourth
input_cases.what_it_shows: CheckHyphens: no hyphens in the third and fourth positions of a label that is not an A-label.

input_cases.label: check-bidi
input_cases.what_it_shows: CheckBidi: a left-to-right label with a right-to-left character.

input_cases.label: check-joiners
input_cases.what_it_shows: CheckJoiners: ZERO WIDTH JOINER outside the context that allows it.

input_cases.label: bidi-formatting-character
input_cases.what_it_shows: A bidirectional formatting character (RIGHT-TO-LEFT OVERRIDE) is disallowed.

input_cases.label: single-label
input_cases.what_it_shows: Not a fully qualified host name.

carried_cases.label: registrable-under-icann-suffix
carried_cases.what_it_shows: A name under an ICANN public suffix, not one itself.

carried_cases.label: private-section-suffix
carried_cases.what_it_shows: A public suffix of the PRIVATE section (a multi-tenant platform) is associated exactly as declared (§5 names the ICANN section only; §11).

carried_cases.label: name-under-private-suffix
carried_cases.what_it_shows: A name under a private-section suffix.

carried_cases.label: wildcard-exception
carried_cases.what_it_shows: `!www.ck` is an exception to `*.ck`: not a public suffix.

carried_cases.label: u-label
carried_cases.what_it_shows: A U-label is not the carried form.

carried_cases.label: ipv4-literal
carried_cases.what_it_shows: An IPv4 address literal (its top-level label is all-numeric too).

carried_cases.label: hyphens-third-fourth
carried_cases.what_it_shows: Hyphens in the third and fourth positions of a label that is not an A-label.

carried_cases.label: icann-public-suffix
carried_cases.what_it_shows: Itself a public suffix of the ICANN section.

carried_cases.label: icann-wildcard-suffix
carried_cases.what_it_shows: Itself a public suffix through the ICANN wildcard rule `*.ck`.

sequence.what_it_checks: The table of §7.2 for a party that keeps state per operator_id, and §9 step 3. `accepted` lists the statements already accepted, in order; `received` is the next one. Results: `candidate`, `idempotent`, `conflict`, `rejected`. Statements are named by their construction label and carry the identity the rule reads.

cases.label: first-statement
cases.what_it_shows: No state for the operator: accepted as a candidate.

cases.label: higher-sequence
cases.what_it_shows: 7 after 1: higher than the highest accepted.

cases.label: lower-sequence
cases.what_it_shows: 1 after 7: lower than the highest accepted.

cases.label: same-sequence-same-digest
cases.what_it_shows: The same statement again: nothing changes.

cases.label: same-sequence-other-content
cases.what_it_shows: Sequence 7 again with a different statement_digest.

cases.label: sequences-are-per-operator
cases.what_it_shows: operator-a has accepted 9; operator-b's 3 is compared with operator-b's statements only.

cases.label: unbind-after-bind
cases.what_it_shows: The unbind (8) is higher than the bind (7).

cases.label: older-bind-after-unbind
cases.what_it_shows: A bind (5) never accepted, lower than the accepted unbind (8): an older bind cannot revive the binding.

cases.label: accepted-statement-again-below-highest
cases.what_it_shows: Sequence 1 was accepted before 7. Presented again with the same digest it is idempotent, although 1 is lower than the highest accepted: the first row of the table decides.

cases.label: conflict-below-highest
cases.what_it_shows: Sequence 7 with a different digest after 8 was accepted: a conflict, not merely a lower sequence.

unbind_precedence_cases.label: accepted-unbind-blocks-lower-bind
unbind_precedence_cases.what_it_shows: §9 step 3: the bind (7) was accepted, then an unbind (8) naming the same host. The bind no longer establishes the binding even if the origin still serves it.

unbind_precedence_cases.label: unbind-of-another-host-does-not-block
unbind_precedence_cases.what_it_shows: An unbind withdraws the association to the host it names and to no other (§7.3).
